walkthroughs.body_html:
Algorithm Design & Problem Solving — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Algorithm Design & Problem Solving brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Algorithm Design & Problem Solving.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique involves breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems?
options: Abstraction
Decomposition
Iteration
Encapsulation

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a trace table?
options: To compile code
To track variable values during execution
To draw a flowchart
To store program output

mcqs.q: Why must a recursive function have a base case?
options: Variables that change type at runtime.
Because the syntax requires it.
To make the function run faster.
Without it, the function calls itself indefinitely, causing a stack overflow.
The ability of different classes to respond to the same method call in their own way.
Variables that change type at runtime.
To make the function run faster.
Having multiple classes with the same name.

mcqs.q: Why is UDP used for live video streaming despite being unreliable?
options: Lower overhead and latency - retransmitting late packets would harm real-time quality.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Because TCP cannot handle video data.
To make the function run faster.
